 Order

This first bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.121/2023 registered at Police Station Sinawal, District Datia (M.P.) for offences punishable under Section 376 of the IPC.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 29.04.2024.

A s per the case of prosecution, prosecutrix aged around 40 years submitted a typed complaint on 07.11.2023 to SHO of Police Station Sinawal, District Datia inter alia alleging that on 11.10.2023, she had gone to a temple in Datia along with her son and grand daughter.
Her grand daughter was not feeling well, therefore, she sent her for treatment along with her son to Datia Hospital.
When she was returning from Sonagir temple, one black colour car stopped near her.

sentences.text: 1 Jaloun proposed to give her lift.
So, she boarded car.
Subhash took her to railway bridge Sonagir and stopped the car.
Subhash committed rape on her in the car.
Subhash left her near railway bridge of Sonagir and fled away.
Her son came there.
She narrated the incident to her son, but due to night and receiving information about her ailing husband, she could not report immediately.
After death of her husband, she had come to report.
On such allegations, Police Station Sinawal registered FIR at Crime No.121/2023 for offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.
Prosecutrix was forwarded for medico legal examination.
No external injury was found.
Statements of victim, her son and other witnesses were recorded.
Applicant was arrested on 29.04.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted on 04.05.2024.
The trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has falsely been implicated in this matter over monetary transaction with Shrestha Sahu through the complainant.
Learned counsel contends that FIR is lodged after delay of almost 26 days.
There is no plausible explanation for delay in lodging the FIR.
As per FIR, the prosecutrix has narrated the incident on same day to her son.
Further, prosecutrix in the statement under Section 164 of CrPC has stated that she and her son had gone up to Police Station Sinawal, but they received call, therefore, they returned home.
If prosecutrix was unable to lodge complaint, her son could have reported the matter.
Her son stated that his father, husband of prosecutrix, died on 24.10.2023, but no report was lodged immediately thereafter.
The unreasonable delay in FIR without plausible reason substantiates possibility of false implication with premeditation and consultation.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 45 years and is in business of mining.

He is sole bread earner of the family, therefore, there is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family,
home and business.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the evidence.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to applicant.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant Subhash Chandra Patel shall be released on bail in relation to Crime No.121/2023 registered at Police Station Sinawal, District Datia (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 376 of the IPC, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.
50,000/- (Rs.
Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, for compliance with the following conditions, :
